ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory real-time screening of all UBOs, directors, and signatories against the UN Security Council Consolidated List, OFAC SDN List, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, UK HM Treasury Sanctions List, and the Korean FIU Political Exposed Persons database. Enhanced continuous transaction monitoring applies because the voice streaming and digital content platform carries a medium-risk AML profile. For every foreign PEP, a senior compliance officer must approve the business relationship, establish source of funds and source of wealth, apply enhanced due diligence, and review the relationship at least annually. Any match or potential match must be escalated and filed with the Korea FIU pursuant to the Act on Reporting and Use of Specific Financial Transaction Information. Domestic PEPs include executive-level public officials, National Assembly members, judges, prosecutors, senior military officers, and senior central bank officials.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Internet Registration Office of the Supreme Court of Korea (IRo) online corporate name clearance portal
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The statutory corporate name must end with the Korean-language suffix equivalent to Yuhan Hoesa (limited liability company). The name is registered in the Korean alphabet, with a permitted parallel transliteration into Latin script for international banking and payment-rail purposes. The doctrine requires a four-tier assessment: (1) pre-clearance of the Korean script name; (2) phonetic transliteration into the Latin alphabet; (3) trademark and service mark similarity search under the Trademark Act; and (4) similarity comparison against all existing registered entities, including abbreviations, Korean-script variants, Latin variants, and widely recognized English trade names.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: On receiving a registry rejection notice, the applicant may file a written objection with the head of the competent district court registry office within 14 days, citing the relevant provisions of the Commercial Act and the Registration of Commerce Act. The objection must include either a proposed amended name or a rebuttal demonstrating no confusing similarity with the cited prior registrations. If the registry court maintains its refusal, the applicant may appeal through the appellate registration procedure to the Supreme Court and may also seek a preliminary injunction against a similarly named entity. A trademark applicant may request reconsideration from the Korean Intellectual Property Office within 30 days if the refusal was based on trademark similarity. All appeal fees are paid by court stamps or online settlement through IRo.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: For a Yuhan Hoesa exclusively operating a voice streaming social application with digital content and no physical retail presence, a virtual office or commercial mailbox is legally permissible for corporate registration under the Commercial Act because Korea does not mandate a storefront for online service providers. Nevertheless, the National Tax Service requires a fixed place of business for value-added tax registration, and most licensed commercial banks reject a pure virtual-office address for business account opening and merchant acquiring. The payment rails of Apple IAP and Google Play Billing do not require a local payment-gateway license. The operator should lease a serviced office with dedicated meeting rooms and a tax-verifiable address to satisfy the NTS and banking substance expectations.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist: (1) confirm the registered address appears on a lease, sublease, or service agreement; (2) post a sign identifying the Yuhan Hoesa at the location; (3) maintain employee workstations, telephony, server or cloud access, and mail handling; (4) make accounting records available at the office; (5) instruct reception staff to identify the exact legal name; and (6) retain the landlord certificate and business registration certificate. Quantified risk: moderate for a first-year online app operator without local employees; estimated inspection probability of 35% during the first two VAT periods, rising to 60% if a tax refund is claimed under zero-rated export rules. A mailbox-only address elevates the risk of rejection and tax investigation to 90%.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea, Act No. 1000, as amended, Chapter VI on Limited Liability Companies (Yuhan Hoesa), Articles 543 to 619; Commercial Registration Act of the Republic of Korea, Articles 14, 21, 32 and related provisions; Electronic Registration of Corporation Act for online registry filings.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registration Division of the Supreme Court Registry Office, exercised territorially by the District Court Registry Office at the company's registered office; for Seoul, the Seoul Central District Court Registry Office, Commercial Registration Section.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Company Registration Application for Incorporation of a Limited Liability Company filed on the prescribed court registry form, together with the notarized Articles of Incorporation and supporting attachments under Article 553 of the Commercial Act.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None. The Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea imposes no statutory minimum paid-up capital for a Yuhan Hoesa. If capital is declared in the Articles of Incorporation, each subscriber must fully pay the subscribed amount into a domestic Korean bank account before registration; the bank's deposit certificate must be attached to the registration application. If no capital is declared, no blocked escrow account or capital deposit certificate is required, but bank counterparties may still require a funding threshold. Non-resident subscribers may contribute foreign currency subject to the Foreign Exchange Transactions Regulations.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
RESOLUTION OF THE FIRST BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF YUHANGHOESA, A YUHAN HOESA UNDER THE COMMERCIAL ACT OF THE REPUBLIC OF KOREA.

The undersigned persons, being the duly appointed and qualified directors of YuhanHoesa, a limited liability company formed under the Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea, hereby constitute the first board of directors. Notice of this meeting has been waived by unanimous written consent of all directors, and the meeting is held in accordance with Article 560 of the Commercial Act. A quorum is present throughout the meeting.

RESOLVED, that the full subscription to the share capital of the Company, as set forth in the notarized Articles of Incorporation, is hereby ratified, adopted, and confirmed; that all contributions have been duly paid into the capital deposit account established for the Company; and that the register of members shall be opened and maintained in accordance with law.

RESOLVED, that the registered office of the Company is adopted as the address specified in the Articles of Incorporation and that the representative director is authorized to execute a lease, register the office, and make any necessary changes within the lawful scope of the Commercial Act.

RESOLVED, that the following statutory officers are appointed to hold office until the first ordinary general meeting of members or until their successors are elected: (a) a representative director, who shall possess full authority to represent the Company in all matters and to execute contracts, instruments, and electronic filings; (b) a director responsible for financial accounting and tax compliance; and (c) an auditor having the powers granted under Chapter VI of the Commercial Act.

RESOLVED, that the representative director is authorized, on behalf of the Company, to open corporate bank accounts with any commercial bank in the Republic of Korea, to designate authorized signatories, and to execute all banking agreements, including online banking, Apple IAP and Google Play Billing merchant account mandates, and foreign currency accounts for cross-border settlement.

RESOLVED, that the representative director and corporate secretary are authorized to file all incorporation, tax, and regulatory registrations, pay all fees, and obtain the certificates of incorporation, corporate seal, and tax registration.

RESOLVED, that all actions taken by the incorporators and initial directors prior to this meeting necessary to form the Company are ratified, and this resolution shall be recorded in the corporate minute book and produced to the Registry Office upon request.

This resolution is unanimously adopted and shall be effective immediately.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation, execution and notarization of the Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed Korean notary public; Korean consulate notary division for overseas execution
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: All founding members must prepare the Articles of Incorporation containing the corporate name, registered office address, object of business in Korean and English, amount of capital, contribution amounts per member, method of contribution, classes of shares, and appointment of directors. Each subscriber must execute the articles by signature or seal and deposit a certified copy with the notary public for mandatory notarization under Article 543 of the Commercial Act. The notary will verify identity, capacity, and the validity of the subscribed contributions. Any non-resident subscriber must provide legalized or apostilled identification and, if applicable, a power of attorney in English or Korean. The notarized articles become the foundational instrument for registration.
required_dossiers: Draft Articles of Incorporation
Valid passports or national ID of all founding members
Corporate registration documents if a member is a legal entity
Certificate of foreign company incorporation and apostille/legalization for non-resident corporate subscribers
Power of attorney appointing a Korean representative
Statement of subscription and contribution schedule
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary refuses notarization due to defective provisions or unverifiable identity, correct the articles to remove ambiguities, re-submit the members' signatures, provide updated legalization documents, and request a written statement of refusal reasons; appeal the refusal through the Korean Bar Association notary inspection procedure or reapply before another notary public.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening of provisional capital deposit account and receipt of deposited capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial bank licensed in the Republic of Korea, including Kookmin, Shinhan, Woori, Hana, Nonghyup or an online-only bank providing corporate account services
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After notarization, the representative incorporator opens a provisional deposit account in Korea under the name of the company being formed or of the subscribers, as requested by the financial institution. Each subscriber who has declared a contribution must wire or transfer the full subscribed amount into the account; the bank will issue a certificate of paid-in capital or deposit balance certificate. The bank will apply customer due diligence and anti-money laundering checks, including verification of source of funds, beneficial ownership, and economic purpose. The deposit must remain frozen until the corporate account is opened after incorporation, and the certificate of deposit must be attached to the court registration application as proof of capital payment.
required_dossiers: Notarized Articles of Incorporation
Passports or IDs of the representative subscriber and all account signatories
Foreign Exchange Transaction declaration forms for non-resident remittances
Certificate of paid-in capital issued by the bank upon deposit
AML/KYC forms and source-of-funds declarations
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank freezes or rejects the account due to incomplete KYC or suspicious transaction flags, supply an enhanced source-of-funds declaration, transaction trail, corporate ownership chart, and explanations to the bank AML unit; if no remedy is achieved, apply to another commercial bank with the same dossier and obtain a certified explanation of the rejection for potential escalation to the Financial Supervisory Service.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of incorporation registration with the court registry office
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Seoul Central District Court Registry Office, Commercial Registration Section, or the District Court Registry Office having jurisdiction over the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the Company Registration Application through the electronic court registration information system or physically at the competent Registry Office. The application must be accompanied by the notarized Articles of Incorporation, minutes or written consent establishing the first directors, certificate of paid-in capital, consent of each director to appointment, identification documents, and the registration tax payment receipt. The registry clerk verifies statutory compliance, the legality of the company name, the accuracy of the registered office, and the appointments of statutory officers. Upon successful review, the registry issues the Certificate of Incorporation Registration and the certified corporate registration abstract, which completes the legal existence of the Yuhan Hoesa.
required_dossiers: Company Registration Application form
Notarized Articles of Incorporation
Written minutes of the organizational meeting or joint written consent of all members
Consent and identification documents of each director and auditor
Certificate of paid-in capital/deposit balance certificate
Receipt of payment of court registration tax and local education tax
Power of attorney for the filing agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues a supplementary order or dismissal, serve a corrective response within the statutory two-week correction period, or three weeks for overseas delivery, amending the Articles of Incorporation or attaching the missing evidence. Refile after correcting errors; if the registry rejects on substantive grounds, file a reconsideration request against the registration decision under the Commercial Registration Act and seek legal counsel to remedy procedural defects.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax registration and issuance of business registration certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Tax Service District Tax Office with jurisdiction over the registered office, together with the relevant metropolitan or municipal tax authority
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within twenty days after the incorporation registration date, the representative director must submit an application for business registration to the competent District Tax Office, unless a shorter period applies to certain electronic commerce operators. The application must state the business category, which in this case is data processing and online content services, the representative's personal data, and the registered office address. The National Tax Service will issue the Business Registration Certificate, assign a business registration number, and register the entity for value-added tax and corporate tax purposes. The application can be completed online through the Hometax portal or in person. The local government may simultaneously issue a local business registrant code; thereafter, the company may lawfully issue electronic tax invoices and claim input VAT.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation Registration obtained from the registry
Notarized Articles of Incorporation
Application for Business Registration on the National Tax Service prescribed form
Copy of the lease contract or title deed for the registered office
Identification documents of the representative director
Corporate seal certificate and company information profile if available
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax office rejects or delays registration because of address inconsistencies or incomplete leases, amend the lease or provide a landlord's consent letter; correct the application and re-submit via Hometax. If the rejection is predicated on a statutory deficiency, submit a written correction and request administrative reconsideration to the district tax office review officer.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Convening the first formal board meeting and activation of corporate governance and bank accounts
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors of the Company; corporate banking department of the chosen Korean commercial bank; company registry for any post-incorporation filings
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After the certificate of incorporation is issued and tax registration is complete, convene the first formal board meeting at the registered office or through a virtual meeting recorded in minutes. The board shall ratify the incorporation, adopt the corporate seal, elect or confirm the representative director and other statutory officers, adopt the bank mandate and electronic banking rules, and approve the issuance of share certificates or the register of members. The board minutes must be signed by the chair and directors. The representative director then presents the tax registration certificate and corporate seal to the bank to convert the provisional deposit account into a corporate account, or to open a new corporate account. All corporate resolutions are finalized and maintained in the statutory corporate register.
required_dossiers: Notarized Articles of Incorporation
Certificate of incorporation registration and corporate registration abstract
Business Registration Certificate from the National Tax Service
Corporate seal certificate and corporate seal registration card
Minutes of the organizational meeting and first board resolution
Director identification documents and register of members
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank blocks account activation pending updated board resolutions or foreign-director documentation, adopt a supplemental board resolution, provide apostilled director passports, and submit a corrected corporate registration abstract. If board quorum issues arise, obtain unanimous written consent in lieu of a physical meeting where permitted and refile the minutes with the registry if required.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Not Applicable; would be the Ministry of Environment of the Republic of Korea if a physical facility were established
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Not Applicable - no physical manufacturing, chemical, assembly, or warehousing facility under ISIC 6311
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not Applicable - no wastewater discharge, VOC emissions, or hazardous waste generation is associated with the digital voice streaming application; server hosting and office facilities, if any, must comply with general electronic equipment waste obligations and local office building fire codes.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not Applicable - no physical production or storage premises requiring Civil Defense fire permit, structural load inspection, or industrial workplace safety approval. The company must nevertheless comply with the Occupational Safety and Health Act for any office premises, including general fire safety maintenance, electrical safety, and emergency evacuation planning.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service (NTS), Republic of Korea - online portal HomeTax (www.hometax.go.kr); Korea Customs Service (Uni-Pass) for cross-border trade clearing
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Incorporate the Yuhan Hoesa with the local Commercial Registration Tribunal (Korean court) and obtain a certificate of incorporation; if foreign capital is subscribed, file a foreign investment report with the Ministry of Economy and Finance or the introduced bank and obtain a foreign investment registration certificate. Step 2: Within 20 calendar days from the date of business commencement, file the Business Registration Application Form with the district National Tax Service office having jurisdiction over the registered domestic place of business. The application must attach: the certificate of incorporation, articles of incorporation, a copy of the lease agreement for the domestic business address, the foreign investor entity's certificate of incorporation or individual passport, and the foreign investment (or foreign currency deposit) certificate. Step 3: After verification, the NTS issues a 10-digit Business Registration Number, which concurrently serves as the Corporate Taxpayer Identification Number and the VAT registration number for all tax purposes. Step 4: If the entity also imports or exports physical goods, obtain a Customs Business Certificate from Korea Customs Service; for pure digital services this step is optional but a customs-based Export Service Report may be used for zero-rating proofs. Step 5: If no domestic presence exists, a foreign non-resident entity that supplies taxable services in Korea must separately register under the simplified foreign operator regime by filing an application with the NTS International Tax Division and receive a special registration number beginning with 'X'.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None (no check-the-box election exists in Korean tax law; a domestic Yuhan Hoesa is mandatorily taxed as a corporation under the Corporate Income Tax Act. A limited group consolidation election under the Framework Act on National Taxes is available only to qualifying 100% (or 90%+) parent-subsidiary groups, not applicable to this single-entity scope).

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value-Added Tax (VAT) under the Value-Added Tax Act of South Korea
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Zero threshold for a domestic Yuhan Hoesa engaged in taxable supplies (registration is mandatorily required from the first day of business and is not turnover-dependent). For a foreign non-resident digital service supplier, a mandatory registration threshold of KRW 100,000,000 of annual Korean-sourced digital supply sales applies.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: All VAT-registered taxpayers in South Korea are obliged to issue and transmit electronic tax invoices through the National Tax Service HomeTax platform using the NTS-certified XML or JSON schema. The invoice data is cleared in near-real time by the NTS Integrated System for E-tax Invoices; there is no additional physical fiscal stamping. For B2C voice-streaming transactions where the customer is a domestic consumer and payment is processed through Apple or Google billing platforms, the app-store operator is treated as a VAT-collecting agent for its foreign branch, and must report the gross sales through its own NTS electronic filing portal. The domestic app provider must nevertheless record each transaction in its VAT ledger and issue an electronic cash receipt in cases where the transaction is not already reported by the payment gateway.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under Article 21 of the Korean VAT Act and the relevant NTS guidance, cross-border supplies of voice streaming services (a category of digital services) qualify for 0% VAT treatment if (i) the service is acquired by a foreign non-resident business or foreign individual; (ii) the service is practically consumed outside Korea substantiated by IP geolocation of the user at the time of streaming; (iii) the consideration is remitted in foreign currency and repatriated to a Korean foreign exchange bank account; and (iv) the supplier retains documentary evidence of non-resident status. The service is deemed to be an exported service and not subject to the 10% VAT when the recipient is located in a foreign jurisdiction and the payment is not sourced from Korea.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Written service contract or purchase order executed with the non-resident customer and specifying the foreign-currency consideration
Commercial invoice issued in the foreign currency, cross-referenced to the bank remittance
Foreign Currency Deposit Certificate issued by a licensed Korean foreign exchange bank evidencing receipt and conversion of the export proceeds
Digital service delivery log and platform-generated copy of streaming usage reports geolocated to the foreign customer's IP address
Proof of non-resident status of the customer, such as a foreign corporate tax registration certificate, passport copy, or beneficiary tax ID in the recipient jurisdiction

If physical goods are bundled in the same transaction (not applicable to pure voice streaming, but required when app is distributed through a physical SDK), the Customs Export Declaration and Bill of Lading shall be added.
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The NTS may audit the zero-rating claim at any time within a 5-year limitation period for negligent misreporting or 10 years for fraud. If the documented foreign currency is not received in Korea within the 180-day repatriation window, the zero rating is voided from the original date, and the NTS will assess the 10% VAT plus inflation interest. Additional penalties apply under Article 60 of the VAT Act: 10% of the underpaid tax for oversight, 40% for non-wilful but negligent misdeclaration, and 80% for fraudulent or concealment-driven claims. Criminal indictment for tax evasion under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act may add imprisonment up to 5 years and a fine up to KRW 100 million. Any refund already obtained through a zero-rated export return must be repaid with interest, and the refund right is retroactively cancelled.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: The Bank of Korea (BOK) as the central bank, together with the Ministry of Economy and Finance (MOEF) as the designated foreign exchange administration under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, with the Financial Supervisory Service (FSS) for bank conduct supervision and the Korea Customs Service for trade settlement data monitoring
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: South Korea operates a liberalised but strictly supervised Foreign Exchange Transactions Act framework. The Korean won (KRW) is freely convertible for current account transactions such as trade in goods and services, royalty payments, dividends, interest, and platform settlement fees; these flows are subject only to mandatory reporting through the Foreign Exchange Information System (FEIS) and do not require prior administrative approval. Capital account transactions, by contrast, remain under a negative list system: inward foreign direct investment must be filed under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act, and outward transfers beyond regulatory thresholds require prior reporting to an authorised foreign exchange bank. There is no statutory surrender requirement for export proceeds in the sense of mandatory conversion into KRW; exporters may retain foreign currency balances domestically or abroad, but the receipt must be evidenced within the statutory collection period. Profit remittance is permitted once the Korean entity files audited financial statements, pays corporate tax, and settles the applicable dividend withholding tax, generally 22% for a non-resident corporate shareholder without treaty relief. The practical friction is documentary rather than regulatory: banks require source-of-funds evidence, beneficial ownership disclosure, and the underlying FDI report before executing a large KRW conversion and outbound remittance.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and its Enforcement Decree, export proceeds must normally be received within six months from the date of export declaration or from completion of the exported service, with extension available through an authorised foreign exchange bank for bona fide trade reasons. There is no mandatory conversion ratio: exporters may keep export proceeds in foreign currency in domestic foreign-currency accounts, but all receipts must be reported via FEIS. If the proceeds are converted into KRW, the receiving bank records the spot transaction under the relevant FX reporting code, and the retained foreign currency is subject to annual foreign-account reporting if held overseas.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account / Basic Operational Currency Account
Capital Escrow Account / Basic Operational Currency Account
Capital Escrow Account / Basic Operational Currency Account
Capital Escrow Account / Basic Operational Currency Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low. South Korea reserves foreign exchange business to authorised foreign exchange banks under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, and fintech electronic money institutions (EMIs) do not hold a banking licence and cannot open corporate demand deposit accounts, execute FX conversions, or operate clearing rails for equity capital and trade settlements. An offshore digital EMI may only provide invoicing, payment-card facilitation, or expense sub-accounting if it partners with a licensed domestic bank, but all legal inbound and outbound settlement flows must go through a Tier-1 authorised bank. Treating an EMI as a primary treasury rail would trigger FEIS non-reporting, bank account freezing, and FSS enforcement risk.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For a foreign-controlled Korean LLC, physical in-branch attendance by the statutory representative is the market norm and is required by most Tier-1 Korean banks under the Real-Name Financial Transactions Act and the aligned FATF AML framework. Remote consular proxy opening is only occasionally permitted when the director's passport and power of attorney are consular-notarised and apostilled, and when the beneficial owner completes a live video KYC interview with the bank's compliance officer and the proxy holder appears physically at the branch. In practice, the statutory representative should expect a physical interview at a Seoul branch during initial onboarding, and an additional enhanced due-diligence review given the medium-risk enhanced classification of a voice streaming and companion social application.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk jurisdiction connection in the shareholding chain or remitter banks with weak AML enforcement, combined with anonymous user funding of voice-streaming content.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified corporate registry extracts showing the complete ultimate beneficial owner chain above 25%, apostilled certificates of incorporation and passports for all shareholders, source-of-wealth statements, audited financial statements of the direct shareholder, bank reference letters from the remitting banks, and the filed foreign-investment report issued by MOEF or the delegated bank.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Mismatch between the declared business of an interactive audio chatroom and companion social application and expected transaction flows, notably high-frequency low-ticket in-app purchases through Apple IAP and Google Play Billing versus large one-off inbound equity injections.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Current Apple and Google developer or publishing agreements, the app's terms of service and monetisation rules, subscriber and daily active user reports, unit economic summaries, server-side transaction logs aggregated by an independent accountant, and the commercial agreements covering voice content licensing, royalties, and broadcaster payout obligations.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident management concentration without a clear local tax, employment, or physical footprint, which is a common shell-company red flag.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certificate of corporate tax registration, valid commercial lease agreement or registered corporate service provider address, local tax agent appointment letter, payroll and social insurance records for any local employees, and a consolidated AML declaration from each shareholder confirming the origin of capital and the commercial purpose of the Korean entity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions and export-control exposure from distributing digital voice content or making tip payouts to prohibited end-users or jurisdictions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Automated IP-geolocation and sanctions-screening logs, the producer and licensor catalogue with export-control classification, contractual restrictions on service delivery to sanctioned countries, a documented country-restriction policy, and a third-party compliance audit report confirming alignment with UN, OFAC, EU, and Korean Foreign Exchange Transactions Act reporting obligations.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound equity capital must be routed through an authorised foreign exchange bank under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act. The remitter should send a SWIFT MT103 in USD or another freely convertible currency with the remittance information field stating 'Paid-in Capital - Foreign Direct Investment' and referencing the FDI report number issued by MOEF/Invest Korea or the delegated bank. The receiving bank credits the foreign investor's capital escrow account, executes KRW conversion at the market rate, and issues the foreign investment certificate after matching the remittance to the board resolution, the FDI report, and the investor's bank reference. Capital verification is completed when the deposited amount equals the declared equity contribution and the bank obtains a written capital release instruction from the investor and the Korean entity.

stage_4.outbound_trade_disbursements: Operational outbound disbursements for content licences, voice AI technology royalties, overseas marketing, dividend remittances, and intercompany service fees are cleared via SWIFT MT103 by the same authorised foreign exchange bank after the applicable FX purpose code is reported in FEIS. For physical trade in servers, sound equipment, or merchandise, commercial letters of credit (MT700/MT710) and documentary collections are compliant clearing rails and must be presented to the domestic bank with transport and invoice documentation. Apple IAP and Google Play Billing settlements arrive as batch clearing-house remittances from the platform operator and should be matched to the platform remittance advices and the underlying user transaction logs before residual KRW liquidity is swept for operating purposes.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore deliverable KRW forward contracts with authorised foreign exchange banks, supported by genuine trade, royalty, or dividend exposure and generally limited to maturities aligned with the underlying cash flow
Cross-currency swaps and currency interest-rate swaps between the Korean entity and a licensed bank for approved debt or FDI capital flows, subject to real-demand documentation
FX options and flex options for hedging USD/KRW or other trade and licensing receivables, with premium payments reported to FEIS

Offshore non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) only on a limited basis, executed through licensed onshore bank international branches or foreign banking counter-parties, and only where the underlying KRW exposure is demonstrated and FEIS reporting is completed

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: March 31 of the following fiscal year (for fiscal year ending December 31)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of 10% of unpaid tax, plus daily interest of 0.02% (annual 7.3%) on the unpaid amount; administrative strike-off not applicable, but tax collection enforcement may be initiated.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Financial Statements Filing with the Court Registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 4 months after the end of the fiscal year (by April 30 for fiscal year ending December 31)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fine up to KRW 5,000,000 (approx USD 4,000) for non-filing; repeated non-compliance may lead to court-ordered dissolution.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Intelligence Unit (FIU) under the Financial Services Commission
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by June 30; or within 30 days of any change in beneficial ownership
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fine up to KRW 50,000,000 (approx USD 40,000) for failure to report; criminal liability for willful omission.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies, an independent certified CPA audit is mandatory if any of the following thresholds are met: (a) total assets ≥ KRW 12 billion (approx USD 10 million); (b) revenue ≥ KRW 100 billion (approx USD 85 million); (c) number of employees ≥ 1,000; or (d) the company is a listed entity or a financial institution. Additionally, companies with total assets between KRW 7 billion and 12 billion may be subject to audit if required by the regulator.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Korean International Financial Reporting Standards (K-IFRS) for companies meeting the audit threshold; Korean Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (K-GAAP) for smaller companies; SMEs may adopt K-IFRS for SMEs.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Beneficial ownership information must be reported to the FIU within 30 days of any change. Additionally, an annual confirmation report must be filed by June 30 each year, confirming the current ownership structure. Share transfers must be reported within 30 days.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 21% national corporate income tax plus 10% local income tax surtax, yielding a combined 23.1% headline effective rate for taxable income above KRW 20 billion
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Various preferential regimes under the Restriction of Special Taxation Act include: 10% to 30% R&D tax credits for technology innovation; a 50% income tax reduction for high-tech enterprise investments in free trade zones; tax holidays for foreign-invested companies under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act in qualified zones; and a technology transfer income tax deferral/exemption for patented or proprietary technology licensing, though no general patent box regime exists.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Corporate Income Tax Return (Form 1: Tax Base and Tax Computation Statement) filed electronically via the National Tax Service (NTS) HomeTax e-filing portal (hometax.go.kr)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual, with a provisional mid-year prepayment return due August 31 for calendar-year taxpayers
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within three months after the fiscal year-end; for a calendar-year entity, the statutory deadline is March 31 of the following year

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 1: Corporate Name and Foreign Registration Status
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name of the Korean entity, domestic business registration number, and identification of whether the entity is a Korean domestic corporation or a non-resident foreign corporation with a Korean permanent establishment (PE).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident foreign corporation that derives Korean-source digital commerce or app streaming income must declare that it is a foreign corporation, disclose its foreign taxpayer/institution number, and identify whether a PE operates in Korea; failure to do so allows the NTS to treat the full global revenue as Korean-source and penalise the understatement.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 4: Head Office, Place of Effective Management, and PE Declaration
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Address of the head office and place of effective management; checkboxes to admit the existence of a Korean branch, agency, or PE.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the voice streaming app is operated through a Korean Yuhan Hoesa and the foreign parent exercises decision-making in Korea, a deemed PE may arise; non-residents should affirmatively state PE existence and allocate profits attributable to that PE, otherwise NTS can reconstruct a PE and impose return penalties.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross Korean-sourced revenue from subscription, in-app purchases (Apple IAP and Google Play Billing), advertising, and audio streaming services.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: All Korean user-derived revenue must be reported in full; costs must be substantiated under transfer pricing rules before deduction. Non-resident filers must attach a schedule showing the app revenue attribution to the Korean PE and cannot offshore the income to a zero-tax jurisdiction without an actual business purpose.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 19: Deductions, Cost Sharing, and Royalty Payments
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Expenses such as hosting, licensing royalties, intercompany service charges, and digital platform commissions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Intercompany royalty and service fees paid to foreign related parties must satisfy the arm's length standard and must be supported by a contemporaneous transfer pricing study; otherwise the NTS disallows the deduction, recharacterises the payment as a dividend, and levies withholding tax of 22% on the constructive distribution.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Schedule 10: Foreign Tax Credit and Tax Treaty Relief
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computation of foreign tax credits and treaty relief for taxes paid on the same Korean-source income in the shareholder or PE beneficiary jurisdiction.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The Korean PE or the beneficial owner claiming DTA relief must attach a Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) from the foreign revenue authority, an OECD-compliant beneficial ownership declaration, and an explanation that the recipient has economic substance; without such documentation the NTS will apply the statutory 22% withholding rate and disallow foreign tax credits.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deduction of tax losses carried forward from prior fiscal years.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Losses may be carried forward for a maximum of five fiscal years and are only allowed if the entity retains an active Korean PE, files returns continuously, and can prove the losses were incurred through genuine Korean business activity; a shell entity that merely stores intellectual property cannot deduct losses of inactive periods.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing within one month of the statutory due date attracts a surcharge of 10% of the unpaid tax; filing more than one month late attracts 20%. Underreported tax is penalised at 10%, fraudulent or intentional understatement at 40% of the omitted tax, plus late-payment surcharges of 0.03% per day (cap 15%). A taxpayer that deliberately suppresses app revenue, destroys books, or disguises Apple/Google billing receipts is subject to criminal prosecution under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act, carrying imprisonment up to 5 years and fines of up to 50 times the amount evaded.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 22% (20% national withholding tax + 2% local income surtax), unless a bilateral tax treaty reduces the rate to 5%, 10%, or 15% depending on ownership and beneficial ownership conditions.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke DTA relief, the non-resident beneficial owner must (1) obtain a valid Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) from its home-country revenue authority, (2) file a non-resident tax exemption/reduction request with the Korean withholding agent or the local district tax office before dividend payment, (3) execute a beneficial ownership declaration confirming entitlement to the income and absence of nominee/conduit abuse, and (4) furnish evidence of genuine economic substance (staff, premises, board decisions) in the residence state. The Korean payor withholds at the reduced treaty rate only after the NTS approves; if statutory withholding was already made, the non-resident can file an amended withholding tax return or a refund claim within five years with the same evidence.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: The domestic statutory withholding on outbound royalties and interest is 22% (20% national + 2% local). Under most DTA protocols treaty rates are: interest 10%-15% and royalties 0%-15%; however, royalties paid for the use of industrial, commercial, or scientific equipment may be taxed only in the residence country under certain treaties. Where the Korean entity is thinly capitalised, excessive interest is recharacterised as a dividend subject to the 22% WHT, and royalties paid to a related foreign licensor without the Korean entity performing a substantive purchasing, development, or sublicensing role may be disallowed as both a deduction and a transfer-pricing adjustment.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: KRW 1 billion in annual cross-border related-party transactions triggering mandatory Local File preparation, and a KRW 100 billion consolidated group revenue threshold triggering Master File documentation; additional disclosure obligations apply to each international transaction exceeding KRW 100 million in the annual corporate tax return.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: South Korea does not follow UAE-style ESR, but applies the substance-over-form doctrine, the General Anti-Abuse Rule (GAAR), and the beneficial ownership requirement under the Law for Coordination of International Tax Affairs. A Yuhan Hoesa must conduct genuine Korean Core Income-Generating Activities (CIGA) such as developer selection, user ToS execution, content moderation, payment revenue collection, and server contracting; a paper entity with no employees, no board meeting records, or no economic activity will be disregarded, its income re-attributed to the foreign shareholder and subjected to 22% withholding plus 20% penalty.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to file the Korean corporate income tax return for the voice streaming app, or deliberately reporting only part of the Apple IAP / Google Play Billing revenue, or attributing Korean user revenue to a offshore shell without any PE declaration.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Article 3 of the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act, imprisonment for up to 5 years or a fine not exceeding 50 times the evaded tax; under Article 80 of the Corporate Tax Act, penalty tax of 40% of the omitted tax plus late-payment surcharges and a prohibition on future tax deduction benefits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The corporate veil is pierced where directors personally ordered, concealed, or profited from the evasion; the director becomes jointly and severally liable for the unpaid corporate tax and civil restitution, can be subjected to a travel ban/blacklisting, and may be arrested and held without bail during criminal tax investigation.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company Substance Failure and Treaty Abuse
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining the Yuhan Hoesa as a tax-haven pass-through with no employees, no physical office, no local board meetings, and no Korean bank accounts, and using artificial licensing or profit-sharing agreements to strip profits to a foreign parent solely to claim DTA withholding tax reductions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The NTS will apply the substance-over-form doctrine and article 21-2 of the Law for Coordination of International Tax Affairs to deny treaty benefits, the shell structure is ignored, all income is recharacterised as a Korean PE profit and assessed with 22% withholding, plus 40% penalty for fraudulent structuring; corporate registration may be revoked.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are held civilly liable for restitution of the assets stripped from the shell, are jointly liable for the reassessed corporate tax, face departure prohibitions while a tax avoidance investigation is pending, and may be personally indicted for fraud and tax evasion, with imprisonment of up to 5 years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Withholding Tax and Tax Remittance Crime
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Sending dividends, royalties, or interest to a foreign shareholder without withholding the 22% statutory or DTA-reduced tax, or withholding but failing to remit the tax to the NTS within ten days after payment, or filing a fraudulent withholding reconciliation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Withholding Tax provisions and Article 12 of the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act, the withholding agent is personally liable for the unremitted tax, a penalty of 20% of the unpaid amount, and criminal punishment of up to 2 years imprisonment or a fine of up to 30 million KRW.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Because the director or officer acts as the statutory withholding agent, he/she must pay the withheld amount from personal assets; NTS attaches a travel ban automatically for cumulative unremitted withholding tax above KRW 100 million, and a criminal conviction disqualifies the director from serving as an officer of any Korean entity and permits seizure of personal property.
